title: Swedish
description: Everyday Swedish: greetings, family, food, numbers, getting around and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
tips: 'Hej' works almost everywhere, with friends and in shops. 'Hej då' means goodbye.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
tips: Swedish nouns are 'en' or 'ett' words: 'en man' (a man), 'ett barn' (a child).

units.title: Food and drink
tips: 'The' goes on the end of the word: 'te' (tea) becomes 'teet' (the tea), 'vatten' stays 'vattnet'.

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
tips: 'En' and 'ett' both mean one: 'en kaffe', 'ett äpple'.

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
tips: The verb comes second in a statement: 'I dag åker jag' = Today go I.

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
tips: 'I morgon' (two words) means tomorrow, 'på morgonen' means in the morning.

units.title: Shopping
units.description: Ask for things, prices and how to pay.
tips: 'Kan jag betala med kort?' – most Swedish shops take cards, and some take no cash at all.

alts: Jag skulle vilja ha den här.
